# Accessibility Requirements Quality Checklist: Final-PR Template Set — Slice 1, the PR Write-up Artifact

**Purpose**: Validate that the accessibility *requirements* for `pr-writeup` are complete, unambiguous, internally consistent, and checkable before code review reads the artifact
**Created**: 2026-08-12
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

These are unit tests for the requirements, not for the artifact. Each item asks
whether something is *written down well enough to build and review against* — not
whether the finished HTML does it.

**Depth**: release gate, because the run prompt frames this as the pass that runs
*before* code review. **Audience**: reviewer at pull-request time, plus the
implementer at the M1/M2/M3 checkpoints. **Focus**: keyboard operation and focus
management, colour independence, token discipline, and consistency between
`spec.md`, `plan.md`, and `contracts/export-payload-contract.md`.

**Interactive clarification was not available** (autopilot run). Defaults applied:
audience Reviewer, focus taken from the six clusters the run prompt names.
Recorded so a later reader knows the questions were skipped rather than answered.

**Result**: 39 items. 14 opened as gaps; all 14 are closed. Each closed item is
re-tagged below to the requirement that now carries the obligation, so the
citation is the evidence rather than the checkmark. Two were closed by the
concurrent error-handling pass and one by the concurrent UX pass; those are
marked to their author so no one re-litigates them.

## Keyboard Operation and Focus Management

- [x] CHK001 - Are keyboard reachability and operability requirements stated for both export controls rather than folded into the artifact-wide focus rule? [Completeness, Spec §FR-027, §FR-034]
- [x] CHK002 - Is the requirement that an export reports its outcome in text, not by colour or animation alone, stated for the failure outcome as well as the success one? [Completeness, Spec §FR-027, §FR-028]
- [x] CHK003 - Are the question disclosure's keyboard-reachability requirements stated for the disclosure control itself, not only for the field inside it? [Clarity, Spec §FR-021, §FR-021a]
- [x] CHK004 - Is the prohibition on positive tab index, focus traps, and unreplaced focus-indicator suppression stated as an artifact-wide requirement? [Completeness, Spec §FR-034]
- [x] CHK005 - Does a requirement fix the question control at the end of its section so tab order follows reading order, with its reason recorded rather than assumed? [Clarity, Spec §FR-023b]
- [x] CHK006 - Do the placement requirement and the section-resolution requirement name the same element, given that the `sec-<slot>` id belongs to the heading and appending to the heading is the placement the spec forbids? **Closed**: FR-023c now states that the id identifies the heading, that the routine resolves from the heading to the section it labels, and that the control mounts at that section's end. [Resolved, Spec §FR-023b, §FR-023c]
- [x] CHK007 - Is the fallback field's obligation to stay focusable and not disabled carried in the spec's own requirement set, rather than only in a Plan-phase contract that the spec itself records will dangle at archive? **Closed by the concurrent error-handling pass**: FR-028 now carries all four steps of the contract's failure path, including "focusable and not disabled" and an accessible name. [Resolved, Spec §FR-028]
- [x] CHK008 - Is "focus moves to the fallback field on failure" stated as a requirement, given that a revealed field nobody is sent to is a silent failure for a keyboard reader? **Closed by the concurrent error-handling pass**, in the same FR-028 rewrite. [Resolved, Spec §FR-028]
- [x] CHK009 - Does the currency requirement bind the moment a status write or a focus move actually lands, rather than the moment the settle callback decides to schedule it? **Closed**: FR-026b scopes the check by effect. [Resolved, Spec §FR-026b]
- [x] CHK010 - Is the exemption for the synchronous refusal path and the no-clipboard path stated against a rationale that survives the deferred announce and focus the named precedent uses? **Closed**: the exemption is withdrawn rather than re-argued. All three shipped templates defer the status write and defer the focus move, so those two paths decide synchronously and land asynchronously; under FR-026b they carry the current token and pass the same check, so no path is unguarded. [Resolved, Spec §FR-026a, §FR-026b, Contract §Invocation currency]
- [x] CHK011 - Are requirements defined for the reading path when scripting is unavailable, given that every question control is script-built and both export controls are inert without it? **Closed**: a new edge case states that US1 survives whole, and that the export region ships hidden and is revealed by the routine that already runs at load, so no dead affordance is left on screen. [Resolved, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK012 - Is the rule that nothing in the file closes a disclosure it did not open carried where the implementer will read it, so a reader's in-progress field cannot be collapsed under them? [Coverage, Contract §A trap that does not reach this port]

## Colour Independence (no meaning by hue alone)

- [x] CHK013 - Is the no-colour-alone rule stated artifact-wide across status, action, and distinction, and required to survive a monochrome print or screenshot? [Completeness, Spec §FR-032, §SC-006]
- [x] CHK014 - Is a verification item's passed-or-pending state required to read as a word rather than as a check glyph's fill? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011d]
- [x] CHK015 - Is the drop of upstream's multi-class syntax highlighting stated as a requirement with its reason, rather than left to the porter's judgement? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011d]
- [x] CHK016 - Is each `before-after` panel required to carry a visible text label, so the before/after distinction does not rest on panel colour or column position after a fill? **Closed by the concurrent UX pass**: FR-018's two-panel shape now requires each statement to open with the word naming its panel. [Resolved, Spec §FR-018]
- [x] CHK017 - Does the `before-after` inventory line instruct the authoring agent to keep the panel labels, in the way the `verification` and `file-by-file` lines instruct it to keep their own carriers? **Closed**: FR-018 binds the shipped sample; FR-017c binds every fill after it, and the inventory line now carries the instruction. The carrier cannot move outside the marker pair, because FR-012 allows one pair per region and FR-013 requires it to delimit a whole subtree, so the inventory line is the only thing that can protect it. [Resolved, Spec §FR-017c]
- [x] CHK018 - Is the question disclosure required to state in text whether its section currently carries a question, so a recorded question is findable without opening all six? **Closed**: FR-021a states it rather than leaving it to "matching the pattern". [Resolved, Spec §FR-021a]
- [x] CHK019 - Are requirements defined that keep a retried task's two entries distinguishable without a colour grouping or a derived ordinal? [Coverage, Spec §FR-019a, §FR-019c, §FR-018b]
- [x] CHK020 - Is every distinction the artifact draws enumerated, so the no-colour-alone rule is checked against a list rather than by inspection? The enumeration is distributed rather than in one list, but it is now complete: verification state and code samples (FR-011d), the two comparison panels (FR-018, FR-017c), the retry pair (FR-019c), the disclosure's carried/not-carried state (FR-021a), and the export outcome (FR-027). [Measurability, Spec §FR-032]

## Token Discipline and Audited Contrast

- [x] CHK021 - Is the requirement that every foreground and background pairing come from the kit's audited set stated, together with the prohibition on relying on colours introduced outside the embedded block? [Completeness, Spec §FR-030]
- [x] CHK022 - Is the subtle-border prohibition stated as an outcome a reviewer can grep for, rather than as a judgement to be re-made at every boundary — the judgement the shipped document-class comparator resolved by using the token nowhere? **Closed**: FR-031a resolves the rule to a checkable outcome for this artifact, on the ground that every boundary this template draws separates content from its surroundings and therefore carries meaning. [Resolved, Spec §FR-031, §FR-031a]
- [x] CHK023 - Is the strong border token named as the carrier for every boundary that conveys meaning, including form-control edges and state borders? [Clarity, Spec §FR-031]
- [x] CHK024 - Does the heading-typeface requirement agree with the embedded kit, which applies the display token to `h1` and `h2` only and records that applying it to every level was a fidelity defect caught against the brand source? **Closed**: FR-033 now scopes the display token to the first two heading levels and names the defect that naming it lower would reintroduce. [Resolved, Spec §FR-033]
- [x] CHK025 - Is the plan's reduction lever accurate about which typeface tokens the kit applies to which heading levels, so "inherit rather than restate" does not license restating the wrong one? **Closed**: the lever now reads "one assignment per level, not one token across all six". [Resolved, Plan §The reduction levers]
- [x] CHK026 - Is heading rank required to ride on semantic level, size, and weight rather than typeface identity, so hierarchy survives the brand face being unavailable? [Completeness, Spec §FR-033]
- [x] CHK027 - Is there a requirement that the pairings the artifact actually uses are recorded, so the audited-set claim is checkable at review rather than taken on trust? **Closed**: FR-030a requires the list with the acceptance evidence rather than as an in-file comment, which discharges the same obligation the shipped comparator discharges in CSS without spending the document-CSS margin. [Resolved, Spec §FR-030a, §FR-042]
- [x] CHK028 - Are the consequences of naming an undefined custom property recorded, so a token typo cannot fail silently into a fallback nobody audited? [Coverage, Spec §FR-033a, Plan §Constraints]

## Labels and Programmatic Association

- [x] CHK029 - Is "labelled text field" defined precisely enough to exclude placeholder text standing in for a label? **Closed**: FR-021a requires the visible label to be programmatically associated and states that placeholder text does not satisfy it, because it is not an accessible name and it vanishes the moment the reviewer types. [Resolved, Spec §FR-021a]
- [x] CHK030 - Is the export status region required to be present from load and outside every fill region, so a fill cannot delete the thing that reports the outcome? [Completeness, Spec §FR-027, Contract §Feedback]
- [x] CHK031 - Are the section anchor and the section's accessible-name source required to be the same identifier, so the exported coordinate and the programmatic name cannot drift apart? [Consistency, Spec §FR-023b]
- [x] CHK032 - Are the export control labels required to name their destination rather than their mechanism? [Clarity, Spec §FR-022]

## Requirement Consistency Across spec, plan, and contract

- [x] CHK033 - Do the spec's own accessibility requirements carry every accessibility obligation the recovered contract states, so none survives only in an artifact the spec records will dangle when the feature is archived? The three that lived only in the contract are now in the spec: the failure path's focus obligations (FR-028), the disclosure's state text and the real label (FR-021a), and the currency check's scope (FR-026b). [Consistency, Spec §FR-029a]
- [x] CHK034 - Is the divergence on capture-control placement recorded with its rationale in both the spec and the contract, so a reviewer does not read it as a violation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-023b, Contract §Where the capture control is mounted]
- [x] CHK035 - Are the accessibility requirements consistent with the headings-outside-the-pair rule, so no fill can delete a heading that an export names or that names a section? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011e, §FR-023b]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [x] CHK036 - Are requirements defined for the monochrome print and screenshot case as a first-class scenario rather than an aside? [Coverage, Spec §FR-032, §SC-006]
- [x] CHK037 - Are reduced-motion requirements scoped to motion the artifact itself introduces, with the canonical blocks' own motion left to them? [Clarity, Spec §FR-035]
- [x] CHK038 - Are requirements defined for the empty export case that prevent the artifact stating a conclusion the reviewer never reached? [Coverage, Spec §FR-029]
- [x] CHK039 - Can the keyboard-only acceptance criterion be objectively verified as written, including the export step and the failure path? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]

## Notes

- All 39 items pass. 14 opened as gaps and each is closed by a named requirement, cited inline above.
- The line cost of the whole pass is **one line**, charged to markup and recorded in both the spec's Reviewability Budget and the plan's re-declared figure. Total moves 757 to 758; headroom to the 800 block is 42. Every other remediation fixed wording, an inventory value FR-014 already makes mandatory, or the placement of a guard FR-026a already budgets.
- The three colour-only carriers ART-002's review found were checked against this port. Two were fixed in that port and their fix is the precedent here: severity reads as a dot count plus the word, and a trade-off reads as a column heading plus a plus-or-minus shape. The third — multi-class syntax highlighting, whose keyword, string, and function classes separate by hue alone — is the one that survived into a shipped template, and FR-011d already forecloses it here.
